extracted.intended_audience: householders, small-scale workshop owners, and general readers interested in domestic motors and nervous-depression/health
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for choosing and evaluating small (domestic/shop) motive-power machines (windmills, water-wheels, small steam/gas/electric motors) with additional medical-discussion content on indigestion as a cause of nervous depression. Focuses on suitability, cost, safety, operation, and maintenance for household and light-industry uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readiness for intermittent work
rubrics_metrics.description: The work for which [a domestic motor] is needed is generally of an intermittent character, and this necessitates a machine that will always be ready for work, or that can be made ready with but little trouble at short notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machines for household use should be immediately available without lengthy startup; design and installation should favor minimal startup procedures and quick availability for occasional tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low expense when idle
rubrics_metrics.description: A machine that is no expense, or but very small expense, when not being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating costs should be negligible when the motor is not running — important for domestic/intermittent uses to avoid continuous overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect safety
rubrics_metrics.description: It needs further to be perfectly safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Household motors must minimize risk to unskilled attendants; safety features and simple fail-safe mechanisms are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economical in use
rubrics_metrics.description: Economical in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running costs (fuel, water, maintenance) should be low relative to the useful power provided; select motors with efficient energy usage for the intended duty cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low first cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Of low first cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial purchase price should be affordable for householders; weigh higher purchase price against lower operating costs (e.g., windmill > steam-engine by 25–50% in some cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple, minimal maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: To require but little care, and that of a kind which can be given by unskilled labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer designs with few moving parts, easy lubrication points, and simple maintenance procedures suitable for lay operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match machine size to user needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The kind of machine that is suitable to the varied needs of these different classes of users necessarily differs in each... In most trades the demand for power is for one of from two to five horse and above, and on the farm a serviceable machine could not generally be much if any less; but in the household that desired is rarely above one horse, and generally under it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose horsepower appropriate to application: household tasks usually <1 HP; workshops 2–5+ HP. Oversizing wastes cost and may be impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for continuous vs. intermittent power
rubrics_metrics.description: When a steady and continuous power is required... the windmill is not suitable; but for all uses in which such conditions do not hold, such as pumping water, it is admirably adapted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use windmills for intermittent, timing-friendly tasks (pumping, occasional workshop use); choose other motive forms (water, steam, gas) for continuous, on-demand power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Windmill regulation methods — centrifugal vs vane-governor
rubrics_metrics.description: Two methods of regulating the extent of wheel-surface exposed to the wind are now in use... centrifugal mills ... many joints on which the wear is very considerable; liability to derangement is greatly increased... The second form ... using the vane-governor, is much simpler in construction, has fewer parts, and is consequently more durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer vane-governor (side-vane) designs for simplicity and durability in domestic applications; be cautious of centrifugal designs due to many moving joints and higher failure risk in high winds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to adjust closing/operating velocity
rubrics_metrics.description: The velocity at which the wheel will completely close can be regulated by the counterweight, which is movable on its arm by means of appropriate connecting rods, from the base of the tower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motor/regulation systems should allow easy external adjustment (e.g., accessible counterweights or linkages) so owners can tune behavior to local winds/loads without disassembling the wheel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability and fewer moving parts
rubrics_metrics.description: This method of regulation [vane-governor] has been found to answer very well in practice, but it has several grave objections... The second form ... is much simpler in construction, has fewer parts, and is consequently more durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs minimizing joints and movable sections will reduce wear and risk of catastrophic failure; for household use prioritize durability over small efficiency gains that require complex mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water-motor economy of water
rubrics_metrics.description: Wheels adapted for use upon house-pipes have to be, first of all, economical of water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose water motors (e.g., Backus-type jet wheels) that use high-velocity small jets to maximize work per unit water; crucial where municipal supply is limited or metered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water-motor freeze-resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: They should also be constructed so that they are not liable to injury by water freezing in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select enclosed casing designs with unobstructed drainage or flow paths so no water remains to freeze; designs that allow water to escape rather than stagnate in the wheel are preferred for cold climates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water-motor low initial cost and small scale availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The extreme simplicity of the motor enables the makers to place it on the market at a very low first cost, varying from fifteen dollars in the case of the seven-inch to two hundred and seventy-five in that of the forty-five-inch double wheel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For small applications (sewing machines, organs) inexpensive small-diameter wheels are available; assess scale and cost trade-offs for larger tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water-motor operating pressure suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The motors are designed to run at any pressure above fifteen pounds per square inch. This is easily obtained, as at most places where there are water-works there is a pressure of from twenty to forty pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify local municipal/service pressure before selecting a water motor; ensure motor's minimum operating pressure matches supply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise control of power delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect control over the supply of water is given by a valve operated by a treadle, which enables the operator to stop and start the machine as readily and quickly as by the ordinary foot-power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control mechanisms that mimic familiar human interfaces (treadle valves, on/off controls) are advantageous for operators accustomed to foot-power machinery; they also conserve resource use by delivering only required power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to light machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: In a similar manner it can be used to drive any sort of light machinery, scroll-saws, dental engines, jewelers' lathes, coffee-mills, etc. One of the uses to which it is peculiarly well adapted is the blowing of organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match water-motor selection to equipment types: sewing machines, small lathes, organs, printing-presses, elevators, etc., are appropriate targets — confirm torque and speed compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local cost-of-operation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of operating these motors depends upon the locality in which they are used... The average charge made by water-boards is from fifty to seventy-five dollars a year per horse-power... In New York and Philadelphia the insufficiency of the water-supply prevents their use at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess local water rates, availability, and utility policy; special commercial rates may be possible if motors are used only intermittently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design innovation trade-offs (e.g., Talley's wave-line wheel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Another wheel ... is capable of being used either as a turbine or an overshot... The sheet of water exerts a continuous pressure upon the wheel instead of moving it by successive impacts... The wheel is said to be quite economical of water, and to run easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider novel designs that combine turbine/overshot features for specific site advantages (variable head, need for continuous pressure) and evaluate claims about water economy and ease of running against field performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spring motors generally impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: For light pieces of machinery ... various sorts of spring motors have from time to time been devised, though none of them seem to have been brought into use. They are not properly motors, and are really quite valueless for the purpose of power, unless it be very slight, as that required in clocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spring-driven motors for meaningful mechanical work (sewing machines require ~400 ft-lb/min). For short-duration tiny loads consider only where other power unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gravity (weight) power impractical except when harnessed by water
rubrics_metrics.description: A weight is a much better device, and yields a large per cent. of the power expended in raising it when it falls. Such an arrangement is, however, a thoroughly impracticable one... The only practicable way of utilizing gravity for motive power is by the water-wheel, where the weight can fall continually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that weight-driven power is theoretically efficient but impractical for continuous use unless coupled to flowing water or similar continual resetting mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symptoms indicating nervous depression from indigestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes described include increased irritability, diminished power of concentration, slower idea flow, poor expression, temper changes, great mental depression, melancholy (worse at night), sleeplessness or abnormal drowsiness, daytime fits of languor alternating with energy, and reliance on alcohol for temporary relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These symptoms should alert clinicians and sufferers to consider digestive causes and lifestyle contributors (overeating, stimulants); avoid self-medication with alcohol, which masks symptoms and causes long-term harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathophysiological mechanism: accumulation of waste/oxygen deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Vital processes are more readily arrested by accumulation of waste products within the organs of the body than by the want of nutriment... The brain may suffer not from lack of fuel but accumulation of 'ash' (waste), and water is essential to remove waste products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnosis and treatment should consider impaired removal of metabolic wastes and oxygenation rather than mere caloric supplementation; empirical muscle experiments show washing out waste restores contractile function and oxygenating solutions accelerate recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment/prevention implication for indigestion-related depression
rubrics_metrics.description: More essential to life than food is water for removal of waste; cramming oneself with food and stimulants may temporarily help but ultimately makes the condition worse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize hydration, moderation of food and stimulant intake, and addressing digestive inefficiency rather than simply increasing caloric/stimulant intake. Counsel against alcohol as a coping strategy.
